A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same transformer-block approximation work, renamed from TBA to TOAST. Their complete main texts and appendices, including tables, figures and equations, support comparison despite substantial revision.

before.justification: v5 reports original representation analyses, image-classification experiments, zero-shot evaluation, cross-dataset transformation-transfer results and approximator comparisons.

after.justification: v6 retains original classification and representation results and reports additional efficiency measurements, sample-size experiments and evaluation with original classification heads.

M1.justification: The closed-form, token-shared linear replacement remains unchanged. v5's explicit MSE-based identification stage is dropped in favor of CKA-based redundancy analysis, with automatic block selection identified as future work. Identity becomes a TOAST option, although the equivalent whole-block skipping operation already appeared in v5's adapted SkipAt baseline.

E1.justification: v6 removes the entire scenario of estimating transformations on one dataset and applying them to another, previously evaluated in v5 Tables 3, 14 and 15. The underlying image datasets remain represented. Zero-shot OpenCLIP evaluation is retained in Appendix A.2.3, rather than removed.

E2.justification: The separate ViT-S SkipAt comparisons in v5 Tables 4 and 16 disappear, but their identity operation remains in v6. Identity also joins Linear, MLP and Res-MLP in the joint approximator comparison, whereas v5 Table 5 compared only the latter three. This changes comparator participation without introducing a new baseline family.

E3.justification: Main approximation fitting changes from 3,000 to 500 samples; block-similarity analysis changes from MSE on 500 samples to CKA on 100. v6 adds GFLOPs/throughput evaluation and original-head controls, revises block configurations, and moves the trained-approximator comparison from ViT-S to ViT-L. The five-epoch linear-probe protocol and 3,000-sample zero-shot setting remain.

E4.justification: v6 adds sample-size sensitivity analysis (Figure 5), original-classification-head controls (Table 12), and accuracy-efficiency analysis (Figure 12). It removes v5's CLS-versus-mean-token check, similarity-metric comparison and cross-dataset transfer analyses. The transformation-complexity ablation is revised, while the PCA and misclassification analyses largely survive with relocation or renumbering.

E5.justification: Appendix A.1.5 newly states that throughput is estimated by averaging wall-clock measurements over numerous iterations, adding limited repeated-measurement reporting. Accuracy reporting continues to use three seeds and ± summaries; no increased seed count or new confidence-interval or significance-testing procedure is reported.

E6.justification: Numerous results are added, replaced or removed. Under the revised sample budget, DEiT-S 10→11 ImageNet1k accuracy changes from 73.97±0.17 to 73.78±0.28; this is not a same-setting performance comparison. v6 adds efficiency, identity, sample-size and original-head results and removes transfer results. Conversely, v5 Tables 8, 9, 11 and 12 remain numerically unchanged as v6 Tables 7–10, and the zero-shot scores are unchanged.

T1.justification: The block-mapping setup and least-squares objective remain substantively unchanged. Displaying the standard CKA formula instead of the standard MSE expression concerns an empirical metric already considered in v5; it introduces no new mathematical reasoning, formal guarantee, assumption or proof.

C1.justification: v5's explicit contribution that MSE identifies redundant blocks and its concluding claim of cross-dataset transformation generalization are removed. v6 instead makes approximation from a few hundred samples a central contribution and incorporates identity mappings into the claimed framework. The central claim of compression without training the replacement or fine-tuning the backbone remains.

C2.justification: v6 adds explanations for sample efficiency and the retained OpenCLIP final-block failure, and identifies automatic block selection as unresolved. It removes the cross-dataset/privacy applicability discussion and shifts the ViT-L interpretation from remaining resource constraints toward deployment benefits. These materially revise the mechanism and applicability discussion.

D1.justification: v6 adds efficiency-measurement implementation details: fvcore for GFLOPs and throughput benchmarking on an H100 with batch size 256 (A.1.3–A.1.5). Model identifiers, approximator code snippets, general hardware disclosures and the statement that code is supplied as a supplementary ZIP remain substantially unchanged.

R1.justification: v6 adds EdgeViTs, EfficientFormer and Better Plain ViT Baselines, supporting its on-device motivation and original-head evaluation. Appendix A.2.3 introduces a first-in-setting novelty claim for training-free zero-shot compression. Most related-work discussion remains unchanged; the additional published DeiT reference represents an already cited work.

P1.justification: The title and method name change, and the abstract, introduction, method exposition and experimental narrative are extensively rewritten. Approximation precedes similarity analysis in Section 3, comparisons are integrated into Section 4.2, and zero-shot evaluation moves to the appendix. These constitute substantial narrative restructuring beyond the scientific additions.

P2.justification: Main tables are substantially redesigned around Identity/Linear accuracy, GFLOPs and throughput. Similarity figures are replotted using CKA, sample-size and efficiency plots are added, and the earlier CLS/metric-comparison displays disappear. Retained PCA and error-analysis figures are rearranged, alongside paper-wide typography and layout changes.

improvement.justification: v6 addresses important validation gaps in v5 through measured efficiency, sample-size sensitivity and original-head controls. However, its new Table 4 contains unresolved contradictions: the original ViT-L ImageNet1k accuracy is 78.55 in one column but 86.32 in others, and its 17→23 results conflict with Tables 2–3. These errors undermine the revised comparison evidence. The PDFs do not establish whether the substantial validation benefits outweigh the loss of reporting reliability.
